transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Holt (Hydra, Head of ML), Sofia Alvarez (Hydra, Platform Eng), Ethan Brooks (Hydra, SRE)

[00:00] Liam: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, quick agenda — do a short recap of last week’s numbers, run through updated tokens per dollar with prefix cache on, then batching tradeoffs and next steps. Priya will share the new numbers.
[00:18] Priya: hey team, i ran the 48-hour pilot trace on the dialogue route with two configs: cached prefixes enabled (auto-KV cache) and cache disabled. Important to note the corpus has heavy prefix reuse ~ 28% of requests share the same 256-token prefix.
[00:34] Priya: raw numbers — with caching enabled we measured ~42,600 tokens/$ on average across the 48h window; without caching it was ~9,400 tokens/$. So roughly a 4.5x improvement in tokens per dollar for this workload. Latency median moved from 110ms to 125ms when caching (small overhead rehydrating kv sometimes), p95 stayed around 320–360ms depending on burst.
[01:05] Marcus: that 4.5x is huge — is that stable or skewed by very hot prefixes?
[01:12] Priya: good q — it's driven by a long tail: top 12% of prefixes are 60% of traffic. When we excluded the extreme hot set numbers normalized to ~3.6x improvement, so still big. Also cold starts (when cache evicts) drop tokens/$ down to baseline temporarily.
[01:40] Sofia: are we talking about prefix caching on the model KV or request-level response caching? i want to be sure we mean the same cash — sorry — cache.
[01:48] Priya: we're using KV/prefix caching in the serving runtime — basically we persist keys for the prefix kv so subsequent continuations skip re-compute. Not a full response cache.
[02:05] Ethan: how about batching? we've noticed with our bursty traffic larger batches save token compute but can blow p95. Numbers?
[02:12] Priya: i tested batch sizes {1, 4, 8, 16} with a target concurrency that approximates Hydra's production pattern. tokens/sec (aggregate GPU throughput) increased with batch size as expected. tokens/sec/$ (normalized by cost per GPU-second) improved from ~9.4k at batch=1 (no cache) to ~28k at batch=8 (no cache). With cache + batch=8 we saw tokens/$ ~86k in warm periods. But p95 latency at batch=8 with bursty arrivals spiked to ~720ms when a request waited to fill the batch.
[03:02] Liam: right — classic tradeoff. batching buys unit economics but hurts tail latency unless you cap wait windows or use dynamic batching. We proposed a latency-first policy for certain routes.
[03:15] Marcus: can Redwood do dynamic batching that respects per-route SLOs?
[03:20] Priya: yes — dynamic batching with per-route max-wait and size cap. For Hydra we recommended max-wait 12ms and max-batch 8 for the "interactive" route; that kept p95 under ~340ms while recovering 2.6x tokens/$ over baseline.
[03:38] Sofia: small practical question — do you have the math for tokens/sec/$? how are you computing it?
[03:43] Priya: simple formulation in the shared spreadsheet: tokens_sec_per_dollar = (tokens_processed / wall_clock_seconds) / ($/second). we derive $/second from our provisioned GPU costs plus amortized infra. For hosted pilot numbers I'm using Redwood internal cost model: example GPU cost equiv x = $0.60/hr -> converted to $/sec. we annotated assumptions in the spreadsheet link we sent.
[04:05] Marcus: ok, please make assumptions explicit. i'd like to map to our internal cloud costs (we're on GCP).
[04:12] Liam: we'll add a versioned sheet that lets you substitute GCP per-GPU/hr.
[04:18] Ethan: about cold cache behavior — how long to warm and how do you recommend keeping hot prefixes resident? eviction policy?
[04:25] Priya: by default LRU with size cap; with the 48h trace warmup to 60% hit rate took ~3 hours for this traffic. If you pin a set of prefixes (we can do pinlist) you can hold the top-n keys in memory — that drops warm-up time to minutes but increases memory.
[04:45] Sofia: memory footprint for pinned set — can you ballpark?
[04:49] Priya: for Hydra's hot-1k prefixes it's about 3.2 GB of KV memory (bloat depends on tokenization settings). we can give the exact number after re-running with your tokenizers.
[04:58] Marcus: what about quantization? we want to know if int8 gives similar tokens/$ improvements without breaking quality.
[05:04] Priya: i did an int8 run (post-training dynamic quant) vs fp16 baseline on your dev prompts. Quality delta on rouge/semantic eval was within 1.5% for most tasks, score regressions clustered on long-range context completions. tokens/sec/$ improved ~1.8x for int8 over fp16. latency median improved about 12%.
[05:30] Marcus: that's promising. can we get an audio or model quality sample set to validate?
[05:34] Liam: yes — Marcus, please share a 1k prompt subset you care most about — we'll run a blinded eval.
[05:39] Marcus: will do.
[05:42] [06:00] Priya: a separate note on network: for on-prem or VPC deployments cross-host KV rehydration added 10–40ms when prefix is remote. if you plan a multi-node private cluster size to keep hot prefixes colocated with inference GPUs.
[06:20] Ethan: on that note, our infra team is concerned about egress and encryption. do you support customer-managed KMS and HSM?
[06:26] Liam: yes for Private we integrate KMS and HSMs; we can show the HSM diagram in the compliance pack.
[06:33] Sofia: will we have audit logs showing token-level request IDs?
[06:36] Liam: yes — the console has per-request tracing and audit logs, and we can export them to your SIEM.
[06:42] Marcus: back to the numbers — the tokens/$ variance in the spreadsheet looked noisy hour-to-hour. is that because of burstiness? caching eviction?
[06:49] Priya: both. bursts cause batching to be more effective but increase queuing. evictions during low-memory periods swing tokens/$ downward. we added rolling 6-hour window and p50/p95 for tokens/$ in the dashboard to make it less noisy.
[07:05] Ethan: what operational guardrails do you recommend for us to avoid tail-bloat caused by big batches?
[07:10] Priya: set per-route latency-first flags: for routes backing interactive UI set max-batch=4, max-wait=8ms; for async background tasks you can use max-batch=16 and a larger wait. also enable early-flush: if the candidate list hasn't filled but latency SLO approaching, flush the batch.
[07:35] Sofia: curious about the cost delta if we move from dedicated hosted to private on our GCP fleet — any ballpark?
[07:41] Liam: it depends a lot on utilization — our model: if you sustain >70% gpu utilization, private tends to be cheaper because infra overhead amortizes. we can run a cost-mapping if you provide instance types and utilization targets.
[07:56] Marcus: i'd like to see a 12-month cost projection with utilization bands (40/60/80%).
[08:01] Liam: noted — we'll produce that for you.
[08:05] Priya: quick callout — we found one prompt route where you were sending long 1.5k token context for simple classification. if you can truncate or offload to a reranker we can save ~22% tokens across the pipeline without any model changes.
[08:22] Marcus: that was us — the legacy service still sends the whole doc. i'll ask the platform team to add a lightweight heuristic to strip content.
[08:30] Sofia: anything on safety or hallucination regressions when we quantize?
[08:34] Priya: minimal for our sample set; we will include targeted hallucination prompts in the next blinded eval.
[08:40] Liam: ok, recap of next steps then. Priya will produce benchmark artifacts (int8 vs fp16, cache/pinned runs, batching sweep) and publish a new sheet. Liam will add the cost projection scenarios. Marcus to share the 1k prompt subset and the production traffic histogram. Ethan to set up a read-only GCP billing view or give numbers for us to plug in.
[09:02] Marcus: timeline check — can we have the locked benchmarks and cost projection by next Thursday (2025-07-31)?
[09:08] Liam: Priya suggested a phased delivery: initial artifacts by 2025-07-25 and locked benchmarks by 2025-07-31. That works?
[09:15] Marcus: yes.
[09:18] Sofia: last question — any immediate quick wins we can do this week that don’t require infra changes?
[09:22] Priya: yes: pin the top-100 prefixes (we can do that from our side for the pilot), and add a truncate heuristic for the classification route. That should show measurable tokens/$ lift in 24–48 hours.
[09:33] Ethan: please do the pinlist then.
[09:36] Liam: we'll follow up with an email and confirm the pinlist we used in the 48h run.
[09:40] Marcus: great, thanks everyone.
[09:43] Meeting ended.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts ("cash" for cache, "K-V" sometimes transcribed as "k v"). Links referenced: shared spreadsheet (link removed), compliance pack (link removed), sample eval deck (link removed).
